paragraphs: Judgment center: the work of education administrators (kindergarten through secondary) is to turn these upstream conditions—the education goals and policies of the district and schools, the needs of students, faculty, and parents, curriculum and instruction and assessment data, and budgets, staffing, facilities, and regulations—into executable, verifiable, and accountable schooling and operating results: first set curriculum standards, performance goals, and school improvement directions according to education goals and regulations, then organize professional development and observe teaching and assess curriculum and materials, then recruit, train, and evaluate faculty and communicate with parents and students, meanwhile prepare and execute budgets and arrange school buses, meals, buildings, and safety maintenance, then liaise with government agencies and businesses and the community and write reports and funding applications, and finally adjust plans according to data and feedback and complete the handover. The key judgment is not whether you can control people, but whether you can hold the four things—goals, data, fairness, and compliance—along the chain of instructional leadership, personnel and home-school relations, and budget and operations and compliance, and leave a verifiable record at every step.

Suitable to try first: willing to be responsible for others' teaching and learning results and to accept questioning from parents, faculty, and superiors; able to switch rhythm among instructional leadership, personnel, budget, and logistics; willing to work within regulations, policy, and budget constraints and handle student behavior, attendance, and safety matters; and able to accept meetings and longer hours driven by the school year and supervision and assessment and budget cycles.

Choose with caution: if you expect this work to be only giving orders, or to discuss only teaching without budgets and personnel, or you are unwilling to work within regulations, budgets, and procedures, avoid responsibility for student safety and fairness and personnel discipline, treat data as a conclusion and make major decisions on that basis, or find it hard to keep patience and professional boundaries under multi-party conflict and public accountability, then the actual work experience will usually not match expectations.

Low-risk check: use the fictional school improvement material and anonymous achievement and budget data provided on this page to complete one paper exercise of writing a school improvement plan's performance goals, measures, data basis, budget, and compliance verification; it only checks whether you are willing to verify item by item against goals, data, and regulations and to mark uncertainty truthfully. The exercise uses fictional material, draws no legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions, and is not equivalent to a principal appointment qualification or position training.
Judgment center: whether education goals, data, and student needs can be turned into schooling and operating results that faculty, students, parents, and superiors can all take up and verify.

Work rhythm is set jointly by the school year and semester, supervision and assessment points, the budget cycle, and board or superior approval; there is more public accountability and many multi-party meetings, and decisions and communication need to leave a trace.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: this page is O*NET-SOC 11-9032.00 Education Administrators, Kindergarten through Secondary. Adjacent positions—training and development managers (11-3041), education and childcare administrators, preschool and daycare (11-9031), education administrators, postsecondary (11-9033), school psychologists (19-3034), and educational guidance and career counselors and advisors (21-1012)—have different objects and authorization; this occupation is also not the same as a primary or secondary school teacher. Principal and teacher appointment qualifications, appointment, discipline, and compliance follow the jurisdiction's regulations and district rules, are not inferred from the position name, and must not exceed authority to issue legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions externally.

AI can be treated as controlled data and paperwork assistance, but generated content cannot be treated as unverified achievement analysis, budget, or compliance conclusions; student data, personnel, budgets, external reports, and discipline remain the responsibility of named responsible persons and the institution.

Fit judgment should combine whether you can be responsible for teaching and learning results, whether you can work with data, regulations, and budgets, whether you can communicate under multi-party conflicts of interest and escalate per the system, and whether you are clear about your authority boundaries over student data, personnel, budgets, and external reports; it is not replaced by a self-assessment of having been a teacher or being good-tempered, and all of this must be confirmed in supervised administrative and instructional leadership experience.

All exercises on this page use fictional material; real curriculum, assessment, personnel, budget, compliance, safety, and discipline decisions must be undertaken by personnel with the corresponding qualifications and in accordance with the jurisdiction's regulations, district rules, and education administration department requirements; individuals must not exceed authority to issue legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions externally, and this page does not constitute any legal, financial, or appointment advice.

The work object of this occupation is the school and district with high-frequency interaction among multiple parties: education goals, policy, and regulations; the needs of students, teaching and non-teaching staff, and parents; curriculum, instruction, and assessment data; budgets, staffing, funding, and procurement; buildings, facilities, school buses, meals, and safety; and supervision, assessment, reporting, and approval arrangements. The output is schooling and operating results that meet education goals and compliance requirements: curriculum and instruction delivered per curriculum standards and performance goals, school improvement plans formed from data, recruitment, training, evaluation, and personnel records completed per the system, funding, procurement, logistics, and facility records executed per budget, and verifiable supervision, compliance, and external reporting records. The basis for judgment is education goals, regulations, data, and district rules, not personal preference or the position name.

Editorial verification suggestion: judgment one: whether education goals and curriculum standards are aligned—whether curriculum standards and performance goals are determined per education goals, regulations, and assessment data, rather than making demands from impressions.

Editorial verification suggestion: judgment two: whether instructional observation and curriculum assessment are evidence-based—whether improvements are proposed per instructional observation and curriculum, material, and program assessment and compliance requirements, rather than judging teachers by personal experience.

Editorial verification suggestion: judgment three: whether personnel and home-school communication follow the system—whether teaching and non-teaching staff are recruited, trained, and evaluated and parents and students are communicated with per procedure with a trace kept, rather than by ad hoc decisions.

Editorial verification suggestion: judgment four: whether budgets and procurement are held—whether preparation and execution and authorization follow the budget, funding, and procurement system, rather than using funds at will.

Editorial verification suggestion: judgment five: whether logistics, safety, and facilities are held—whether arrangements and inspections follow the requirements for buildings, facilities, school buses, meals, safety, and maintenance, rather than remedying things afterward.

Editorial verification suggestion: judgment six: whether data, compliance, external reporting, and discipline stay within boundaries—whether data use follows regulations, data permissions, privacy, and student record requirements, without exceeding authority to issue legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions externally, and with consultation and reporting per the system on anomalies.

US BLS says principals work year-round with no summer vacation, some more than 40 hours, and evening and weekend events are required; O*NET tasks include home-school communication, instructional observation, personnel, budgets, and safety, and the division of labor differs by position. Chinese work rhythm and authority cannot be derived directly from US working hours.

The work of education administrators (kindergarten through secondary) can be divided into three connected but independent work faces. The first is instructional and curriculum leadership: observe teaching methods and review learning materials to assess and unify curriculum and instruction, work with teachers to set and maintain curriculum standards, mission, and performance goals, determine course offerings and scheduling and staffing and facility needs, assess curriculum and instruction and program effectiveness and efficiency and compliance, organize professional development for teachers and administrators and support staff, prepare school improvement plans based on student achievement data, and approve new programs or propose modifications for the school board or superior approval. The second is students, personnel, and home-school relations: provide students with academic, behavioral, attendance, and pathway guidance, communicate education policy and student behavior and learning issues with parents and teaching and non-teaching staff, enforce discipline and attendance rules, recruit, train, and evaluate teaching and non-teaching staff and make personnel recommendations, guide and support administrative staff and special education related activities, and coordinate extracurricular activities and student clubs and events. The third is budget, operations, and compliance: prepare and submit budgets and funding applications and determine the allocation of funds, materials, and equipment and authorize procurement, arrange school buses, meals, facility use, building maintenance, safety, and security, interpret government regulations and develop compliance and facility safety and maintenance plans accordingly, liaise with federal, state, and local agencies and track policy, develop business and cooperative and school-enterprise and community programs, write publicity material and manuals and publications, and supervise student drop-off and pickup. All three work faces proceed within education goals, regulations, data, and district rules.

When comparing, verify item by item against the service object, authorization, compliance basis, and output, and do not swap by institution or job title; verify the actual position and jurisdictional authority: management duties may include decisions on budget allocation, procurement authorization, and recruitment and evaluation, and cannot be equated with unlimited legal judgment or financial or personnel discipline authority; for Chinese public schools, also verify the responsibility and authority list, school autonomy, and deliberation and decision-making system under Articles 24/26 of the 2026 measures.
Core purpose

Turn education goals and student and teaching and non-teaching staff needs into executable, verifiable, and accountable schooling and operating results: clear curriculum and teaching goals, evidence-based data and compliance, personnel and home-school relations per the system, budgets and logistics held, and reports and discipline within boundaries.

Core purposes of adjacent positions: training and development managers improve corporate employee ability and performance; preschool and daycare administrators ensure the operation of preschool and daycare institutions; postsecondary education administrators ensure academic and administrative operation of colleges and universities; school psychologists ensure student psychological and learning support; educational guidance and career counselors help students with academic and career planning.
Main object and basis

The object is education goals, policy, and regulations; students, teaching and non-teaching staff, and parents; curriculum, instruction, and assessment data; budgets, funding, and procurement; buildings, facilities, school buses, meals, and safety; and supervision, assessment, reporting, and approval arrangements; the basis is education goals, regulations, data, and district rules.

Objects and bases of adjacent positions: corporate employees and training needs (corporate training and human resources systems); preschool and daycare institutions and children (preschool education and daycare regulations); colleges and their faculty and students and academic affairs (higher education regulations and institutional rules); student psychology and learning (psychological assessment and ethics standards); students' academics and careers (further education and employment guidance standards).
Core process

Instructional and curriculum leadership → students and personnel and home-school relations → budget, operations, compliance, and reporting (including professional development, school improvement, and inspection).

Processes of adjacent positions: training needs analysis—curriculum development—implementation and evaluation (training and development managers); enrollment and childcare—staffing and safety—parent communication and compliance (preschool and daycare); academic and administrative affairs and resource allocation (postsecondary administration); assessment—intervention—referral and records (school psychologists); testing—counseling—planning and referral (educational guidance and career counselors).
Main output

Curriculum and instruction delivered per curriculum standards and performance goals, school improvement plans formed from data, recruitment and training and evaluation and personnel records completed per the system, funding and procurement and logistics and facility records executed per budget, and verifiable supervision and compliance and external reporting records.

Outputs of adjacent positions: corporate training plans and effectiveness evaluations; institutional operation and childcare and safety and compliance records; college academic and administrative and resource records; student psychological assessment and intervention records; student academic and career guidance records.
Responsible party

This occupation is responsible for organizing instruction, personnel, budgets, and logistics per education goals, regulations, and data and for student data, reports, and compliance; the school board, superior education administration department, and competent department bear management responsibility for policy and budget approval and personnel discipline and compliance conclusions per regulations and systems.
Responsibilities of adjacent positions: borne by each institution's responsible persons and professionals per their own regulations and systems, with different authorization bases.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with teachers, teaching and non-teaching staff, parents, students, the superior education administration department, the school board, and logistics, safety, psychology, and counseling staff, and adjust priorities per the school year and supervision and assessment and budget points; student safety, data, personnel, budget, and out-of-authority matters are consulted and reported per the system.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: with human resources and corporate departments (training); with parents, health, and community (preschool and daycare); with departments, faculty, students, and academic affairs (postsecondary administration); with teachers, parents, and medical services (school psychology); and with teachers and further education and employment agencies (guidance and counseling).
Conclusion boundaries

Do not: determine curriculum and performance goals without education goals, regulations, and data; observe teaching and assess curriculum without following the system; recruit, evaluate, and make personnel recommendations without following procedure; prepare and execute without the budget and procurement system; arrange and inspect without the requirements for buildings, facilities, school buses, meals, and safety; use student and personnel data without data permissions and privacy; or issue legal or financial or personnel discipline conclusions externally beyond authority.
The boundaries of adjacent positions are determined by their own object, regulations, and institutional rules; similar institution or job titles do not mean duties can be interchanged.
In this work, which judgments are most prone to error, and how should they be verified?

Common errors cluster in four categories: first, education goals are disconnected from curriculum standards and performance goals, making teaching and assessment requirements inconsistent and improvement unfounded; second, teaching and programs are assessed by impression rather than data and observation, distorting decisions and causing teacher attrition; third, personnel, home-school relations, budgets, and procurement are handled without the system, procedures, and budget constraints, creating compliance, fairness, and interpersonal risks; fourth, student data, reports, and discipline go out of bounds or logistics, safety, and facilities are not held, creating privacy, safety, and accountability risks. The verification method is that each item has a reviewable basis: curriculum standards and performance goals and school improvement plans, instructional observation and curriculum assessment and compliance records, recruitment and training and evaluation and personnel recommendation records, budget and procurement and logistics and facility and safety records, and student data and reports and discipline and compliance records, rather than memory or verbal understanding.

Are recruitment, training, evaluation, personnel recommendations, and student behavior and attendance handling done per procedure with a trace, rather than by ad hoc decisions?

In a student safety incident, provide immediate rescue and protection and report promptly per applicable law and the system, without delaying to gather evidence or fill in records first; Article 52 of the Preschool Education Law for kindergartens requires immediate protection and reporting to public security, education, and other departments. When safety allows, retain evidence and records; data leaks, budget or personnel overreach are handled separately per the actual incident and statutory authority, and the scope of suspension and the deciding body are verified against the real system. China's 2026 revised Measures for the Administration of Primary and Secondary School Leadership applies under Article 2 to public school leadership teams, including kindergartens, with other legal provisions taking precedence; Article 6 generally requires a bachelor's degree or above, the corresponding teacher qualification, and an appointed professional and technical post at level one or above in primary and secondary schools, with high school principals requiring senior level or above; principals generally need 5 or more years of education and teaching experience, and promotion to the top post from within a school generally requires 2 or more years as a deputy or 3 or more years at the middle level. Education requirements may be relaxed for kindergartens and primary schools in difficult and remote areas under conditions, with Article 7 providing additional special relaxation. Article 6 requires obtaining a qualification certificate from the appointment qualification training, and those who do not meet the requirements under special circumstances must complete it within 1 year of promotion; Articles 8 to 11 provide that selection is generally by internal recommendation or external assignment, and may also be by competitive appointment or open selection, and this cannot be uniformly rewritten as open recruitment of new employees. Article 2 of China's Preschool Education Law defines preschool as from age 3 to before entry into primary school; Articles 37 to 38 require kindergarten principals to have the specified teacher qualification, a college degree or above, and 5 or more years of kindergarten teaching or management experience, with founders or decision-making bodies appointing and engaging them per law and filing with the county-level education department, and participation in principal position training. Public kindergartens also verify the 2026 leadership measures and the legal priority boundary; US kindergarten and Chinese kindergartens do not correspond one-to-one, and daycare and all education management positions cannot be uniformly subject to these conditions.

outlook_evidence.metric: Training and appointment qualification and compliance paths
outlook_evidence.value: The typical US BLS education for elementary and secondary school principals is a master's in education administration/leadership, with related work experience classified at 5 years or more; O*NET new-hire education feedback is 62% master's, 27% bachelor's, and 10% post-master's certificate, which is not a statutory threshold for every position. Most states require a state license for public school principals, with conditions often including a master's degree, examinations, and a background check, and some states have alternative paths; private school principals do not need a state-issued principal license, which does not mean other legal or employer conditions are waived. China's 2026 revised Measures for the Administration of Primary and Secondary School Leadership applies under Article 2 to public school leadership teams, including kindergartens, with other legal provisions taking precedence; Article 6 generally requires a bachelor's degree or above, the corresponding teacher qualification, and an appointed professional and technical post at level one or above in primary and secondary schools, with high school principals requiring senior level or above; principals generally need 5 or more years of education and teaching experience, and promotion to the top post from within a school generally requires 2 or more years as a deputy or 3 or more years at the middle level. Education requirements may be relaxed for kindergartens and primary schools in difficult and remote areas under conditions, with Article 7 providing additional special relaxation. Article 6 requires obtaining a qualification certificate from the appointment qualification training, and those who do not meet the requirements under special circumstances must complete it within 1 year of promotion; Articles 8 to 11 provide that selection is generally by internal recommendation or external assignment, and may also be by competitive appointment or open selection, and this cannot be uniformly rewritten as open recruitment of new employees. Article 2 of China's Preschool Education Law defines preschool as from age 3 to before entry into primary school; Articles 37 to 38 require kindergarten principals to have the specified teacher qualification, a college degree or above, and 5 or more years of kindergarten teaching or management experience, with founders or decision-making bodies appointing and engaging them per law and filing with the county-level education department, and participation in principal position training. Public kindergartens also verify the 2026 leadership measures and the legal priority boundary; US kindergarten and Chinese kindergartens do not correspond one-to-one, and daycare and all education management positions cannot be uniformly subject to these conditions.

subject.summary: Education administrators, kindergarten through secondary (US O*NET-SOC 11-9032.00, Education Administrators, Kindergarten through Secondary) are the schooling and instructional leadership positions for kindergarten through secondary education: planning, directing, or coordinating the academic and administrative and auxiliary activities of kindergartens and elementary and secondary schools; the work includes determining curriculum standards and performance goals and school improvement directions per education goals and regulations and data, observing teaching and reviewing learning materials to assess and unify curriculum and instruction, working with teachers to set curriculum standards and mission and performance goals, determining course offerings and scheduling and staffing and facility needs, organizing professional development, providing students with academic and behavioral and attendance guidance and enforcing discipline and attendance rules, communicating with parents and faculty, recruiting, training, and evaluating faculty and making personnel recommendations, preparing and submitting budgets and funding applications and authorizing procurement, arranging school buses and meals and facilities and building maintenance and safety, interpreting government regulations and developing compliance plans, liaising with government and businesses and the community and writing reports, and supervising student drop-off and pickup. US basis: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 105,870 US dollars per year (that source provides only the median and does not provide the 10/25/75/90 percentiles or an hourly basis); the O*NET summary page gives about 333,300 employed in 2024, a 2024—2034 projection of Decline (Decline, -1% or lower), and about 20,800 average annual openings for 2024—2034; the preparation level is Job Zone Five (SVP 8.0 and above), the education feedback is 62% master's degree and 27% bachelor's degree and 10% post-master's certificate, the interest code is SEC, and there are 33 tasks. Mainland China basis: the appointment qualification, engagement, assessment, and training of primary and secondary school principals and related management positions follow the Education Law and the Compulsory Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the relevant provisions of the education administration department, and doing education and teaching work in primary and secondary schools requires obtaining the corresponding teacher qualification per the Teachers Law and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications of the People's Republic of China. Public statistics have no occupation-level wage basis corresponding to this occupation established, and this page truthfully keeps the gap, with the industry average wage serving only as a visible industry proxy.
